A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same XTF study, with 30 complete pages and Appendices A–F. Text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: V3 reports original fine-tuning experiments, benchmark results, ablations, and computational measurements in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: V4 retains the original fine-tuning experiments, benchmark results, ablations, and computational measurements in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same reasoning-importance, knowledge-novelty, and task-relevance scoring mechanisms, filtering thresholds, and masked-token training loss.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, CodeExercise/HumanEval, and PubMedQA, plus NuminaMath-CoT/MATH-500 and FIQA in Appendix C.1. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain CA, Normal, doubled epochs, DF, DA, SLM, and TC. Figure 5 retains CA and Normal as comparators. Appendix B.2 describes identical baseline implementations.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendices B–C retain the same models, full-parameter/LoRA settings, data quantities, training budgets, validation-based selection, accuracy evaluation, and pass@k metrics.

E4.justification: The attribute ablations, threshold sensitivity experiments, computational analyses, score distributions, and token-filtering examples are unchanged, including Table 2, Figure 6, Tables 5–7, and Appendix F.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-estimate performance reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the XTF evaluations.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are identical throughout. For example, XTF's average accuracies remain 45.7% and 37.1% in Table 1, and 38.3% and 19.3% in Table 4.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations in Section 3, the assumptions, theorems, and proofs in Appendix A, and the Otsu derivation in Appendix B.1 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical scientific claims about token-level noise, the three-attribute XTF framework, and its empirical benefits. Publication metadata does not alter these contributions.

C2.justification: The interpretations of attribute complementarity and model-dependent benefits are retained. Section 5's computational limitations, Appendix A.9's theoretical caveats, and Appendix F's qualification about imperfect filtering are unchanged.

D1.justification: Baseline implementation details, Table 3 hyperparameters, precision and hardware disclosures, and scoring resource measurements are identical. No code or data access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-gap discussion, and the reference list retain the same cited works and positioning relative to prior methods.

P1.justification: V4 specifies Qiuzhen College within the Tsinghua affiliation, adds equal-contribution and corresponding-author information, and adds the ICLR 2026 publication header. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V4 adds a running publication header, removes printed page-number footers, and slightly reflows page 1, moving one introduction line to page 2. Figures, tables, captions, and their placements are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V4 clarifies author information and adds publication metadata, while removing printed page numbers and slightly reflowing the opening pages. The scientific argument, evidence, theory, limitations, and reproducibility information are identical, so these limited administrative and layout edits do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
